It is a Meccan surah.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

As for His saying: ﴿Indeed, if You leave them, they will mislead Your servants﴾, meaning: if You leave any of them alive, they will mislead Your servants, that is, those whom You will create after them. ﴿And they will not beget except a wicked, ungrateful one﴾, meaning: wicked in deeds and disbelieving in heart. This was due to his experience of them and his remaining among them for a thousand years minus fifty years.

Then he said: ﴿My Lord, forgive me and my parents, and whoever enters my home as a believer﴾. Al-Dahhak said: this means my mosque. There is no barrier to taking the verse according to its apparent meaning, namely that he prayed for everyone who entered his house while being a believer. Imam Ahmad has said:

Abu 'Abd al-Rahman told us, Haywah told us, Salim ibn Ghaylan informed us that al-Walid ibn Qays al-Tujibi informed him that he heard Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, or from Abu al-Haytham, from Abu Sa'id, that he heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Do not keep company except with a believer, and let none eat your food except a pious person."

Abu Dawud and al-Tirmidhi also narrated it from the hadith of 'Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak, from Haywah ibn Shurayh, with the same wording. Then al-Tirmidhi said: We only know it through this chain.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And for the believing men and believing women﴾, it is a supplication for all believing men and women, and this includes both the living among them and the dead. For this reason, such supplication is recommended, following the example of Noah, peace be upon him, and in accordance with what has come in the reports and the well-known, legislated supplications.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And do not increase the wrongdoers except in destruction﴾. Al-Suddi said: except in ruin. Mujahid said: except in loss, meaning in this world and the Hereafter.

End of the commentary on Surah "Nuh" [peace be upon him, and to Allah belongs all praise and grace].
